_readme: Colour code: [[r:...]] RED = best guess, not yet confirmed by owner. [[c:...]] CYAN = new idea suggested by Claude. Plain = confirmed.
name: Former Wesleyan chapel

layers.essential_history: Red-brick frontage with a circular window and a Wesleyan stone. [[r:It is now a private home. An earlier note says it replaced a smaller Church Street chapel built in 1808, which has not been checked.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[r:Deeper history for this stop is still to be written.]]
layers.mystery: [[r:Journal page: the messenger, Anne Fletcher, is known to have come back from the dispatch room by a longer way than she should have. The chapel you see today is far newer than the story, which is set in the 1600s. It is only here to unlock the page.]]

puzzle.title: The stone
puzzle.intro: [[r:Look at the front of the building from the public road. Do not go through any gate.]]
puzzle.question: [[r:What year is shown on the stone of the former Wesleyan chapel?]]
hints: [[r:Look for a stone set into the red-brick front of the building.]]
[[r:The year is four digits, on the stone that mentions the Wesleyans.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[r:If you cannot read the stone, use the photo shown at the top of this stop.]]

directions_to_next: [[r:The next stop is the Old Bakehouse, a short way along the road. Exact directions are still to be supplied, and stops 4 onwards are still being written.]]
private_note: This is a private home. Look from the road only.
notes: Never present the 1881 building as existing in the 1600s.
